taxonomy:
## Taxonomy of grid-based logic games (from the provided rules only)

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; bulbs illuminate along rows/columns until black squares/frame; no bulb illuminates another bulb; every white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color some cells black; numbered cells count white cells to nearest black cell or frame (horizontally + vertically); numbered cells must remain white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold-bordered rectangles) contain a number of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.

### B) Loop / path drawing games (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers; loop doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; must pass all white-circle cells with area-wise straight/turn consistency; must not pass black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circle cells; white circles require straight-through with a right-angled turn in an adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; loop passes through arrow cells; wind direction from black cells restricts movement (can’t advance against wind); special side-wind bending constraints.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop; must pass all black circles with the circle as midpoint of the straight segment through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each room visited exactly once; in each room loop goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through all “gates” (dotted lines); each gate passed once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order/direction.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop; loop does not pass through black cells or numbered cells; numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

### C) Number-placement / arithmetic filling games (no explicit loop requirement)
- **Chained Block**: Fill black-cell blocks; consecutive black cells form blocks; each block has one number or “?”; blocks in corner contact form chains; all blocks part of a chain; no more than one block of same size/shape in a chain.
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; black orthogonally connected cells form rectangles/squares; white orthogonally connected cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate size of the area containing the cell.
- **Double Choco**: Partition grid into blocks via solid lines; each block contains two same-form areas (white + gray); number indicates half the block’s cells of that color; block can contain any number of numbered cells.
- **Evolomino**: Draw/assign polyomino-like blocks on arrows; each block is a group of squares connected orthogonally; each block contains exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow path must pass through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks grow by adding one square without rotation/flip.
- **Five Cells**: Partition into blocks of exactly five cells; no blocks of size 0–4 or 6+; numbers indicate how many lines of a block surround a cell (including outer frame); lines surround cells and can’t enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; partition into blocks; each block filled with same number; block size equals the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges; number of bridges equals island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/other bridges; bridges form a continuous link.
- **Hebi**: Place sequential snake numbers 1(head) to 5(tail) in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snake parts can’t be in squares adjacent to next black square/rim (attack rule); black squares’ numbers indicate nearest snake distance in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered areas are territories; territory numbers indicate how many more of one mark type it gets (with cases where — and | counts are equal); “—” extends >3 cells horizontally but ≤2 vertically; “|” extends >3 cells vertically but ≤2 horizontally.
- **Kurodoko**: (also fits A) but core is number-based black/white placement with connectivity and non-touching constraints.
- **Kurotto**: Color some cells black; circle number equals sum of continuous black cells extending vertically and horizontally from that circle; empty circles may have any number; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, color four consecutive squares (tetromino); similarly shaped rotated/reversed tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger colored squares.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; each cell has only one digit.
- **Norinori**: Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares.
- **Nurimeizu**: Paint walls to form a maze from S to G using only white cells; rooms are bold-bordered; all cells in a room are painted or left white; white cells can’t be entirely cut off by painted cells and can’t form a loop; rooms containing S, G, ○, △ can’t be painted; all ○ cells lie on shortest path from S to G; no △ on shortest course; black/white can’t cover 2×2 or larger squares.
- **Nurimisaki**: Circle cells remain white and are “Misaki”; non-circle white cells can’t be Misaki; a white Misaki cell has exactly one adjacent white cell and all other adjacent cells are black; circle numbers indicate how many white cells form a straight line from the Misaki; empty circles allow any straight-line length; all white cells connected; no 2×2 group of cells can be all black or all white.
- **Makaro**: Fill empty cells with numbers; bold-bordered rooms; each room contains all numbers up to the number of cells starting from 1; in arrow black cells, the biggest number among up to four neighboring cells is placed in the cell the arrow points at; a number can’t be next to the same number in another room.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black/white; numbers indicate count of continuous white cells; each white area contains only one number and is separated by black cells; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; each block is one or more shaded cells connected orthogonally; number (if given) indicates block size; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 group entirely shaded.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils from the tip; pencil is a straight group of one or more cells with tip at one end; line from tip goes through cell centers horizontally/vertically/turning; numbered cells give pencil length; a pencil may contain multiple numbers; line from tip goes through as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Ripple Effect**: Bold-bordered rooms; fill empty cells with consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Satogaeri**: Bold-bordered countries; move circles orthogonally so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; circles without numbers may move any distance but some don’t; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (four kinds); cannot place in black squares; uncovered white cells must form a rectangle or square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains only one number showing the number of cells in the rectangle.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms are bold-bordered; number in a room shows number of continuous black cells in that room; rooms with no number any; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones are dropped straight down (after deleting colored cells), stones must fill bottom half without empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Sudoku**: Place digits 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all digits 1–9.
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles; color tiles; diagonal-line cell number indicates how many black cells must be to the right or downward along the diagonal’s line/column until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored; solution shows outline of an object.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells containing numbers cannot be colored; (additional constraints appear in the provided text but are not fully visible beyond this rule set).
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; each move shown by an arrow whose tip is in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend and don’t cross other white circles or other arrows’ lines; number in a gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas may have any sum total but at least one circle must enter a gray area.
- **Yajilin**: (also fits B) but core is loop + number/arrow constraints.

### D) Black/white region connectivity & separation games
- **Hitori**: Color cells so no number appears more than once in any row/column; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurodoko**: (also fits A) black non-touching + all white connected + numbered distance constraints.
- **Nurikabe**: Black wall connectivity + white area numbering + no 2×2 black.
- **Nurimeizu**: Maze connectivity from S to G using white cells; white not loop; rooms painted/white constraints; no 2×2 coverage by black/white.
- **Nurimisaki**: White connectivity; Misaki local adjacency constraints; no 2×2 all-black or all-white.
- **Nuritwin**: Shaded connectivity across regions; two same-size blocks per region; no orthogonal touching between the two blocks; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Heyawake**: Painted cells non-connecting orthogonally; white connectivity/separation constraints via room stretching and separation by painted cells.
- **Usowan**: (partial in provided text) colored vs numbered-cell restriction plus adjacency/separation constraints are referenced but not fully visible.

### E) Bridge/graph connection games (non-loop, but connectivity via edges)
- **Hashiwokakero**: Bridges between islands; continuous link between all islands; bridge multiplicity limited; no crossing.
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally/with turns; lines can’t cross/branch; lines can’t go through numbered cells.
- **Hebi**: Snake numbering is a sequential connected structure with non-touching constraints (territorial fights).

### F) Tiling / partitioning games (divide grid into regions/blocks)
- **Chained Block**: Blocks of consecutive black cells; chain formation via corner contact; uniqueness of block shapes in a chain.
- **Double Choco**: Partition into blocks with matching white/gray shapes.
- **Evolomino**: Blocks along arrows; each block is a connected set of squares; growth rule along arrow route.
- **Five Cells**: Partition into blocks of exactly five cells.
- **Fillomino**: Partition into blocks filled with same number; block size equals number; same-sized blocks can’t touch.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (not a partition, but uses island/bridge structure)
- **Nurimeizu**: Rooms partitioned by bold lines; each room painted or white.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms partitioned by bold lines.
- **Shikaku**: Rectangles partition the grid.
- **Slitherlink**: Dots/lines create a loop but also uses cell-based numeric constraints.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms partitioned by bold lines.
- **Tilepaint**: Tiles partitioned by bold lines.
- **Satogaeri**: Countries partitioned by bold lines.
- **Suraromu**: Gates are dotted segments; loop passes them (not a partition, but uses special marked segments).

### G) Sudoku-like constraint grids (rows/columns/block uniqueness)
- **Sudoku**: Standard row/column/3×3 block digit completeness.

### H) “Snake” / ordered sequence games
- **Hebi**: Sequential snake parts 1→5 with directional attack constraints.
- **Nagareru**: Loop with direction and wind constraints (directional movement rule).
- **Pencils**: Ordered “pencil” structure from tip with length constraints (not a snake, but a directed structure).

If you want, I can also reorganize this taxonomy into a smaller set of top-level categories (e.g., “loop”, “fill”, “partition”, “connectivity”) while keeping the same game list.
